messages:
maya.g: noticed a throughput drop on the multi-GPU baseline when we turned on gradient checkpointing (PP+TP stacks) in the nightly run. Was ~11% lower p50 throughput and spikes in all-reduce time. cc @alex.k @samir

alex.k: yup saw that in the dashboard. latency SLOs still OK but unit cost went up. any quick profiler traces?

maya.g: grabbed a short nvprof/nvtx capture from the failing config. small summary: compute time per stage up ~20%, but all-reduce latency distribution widened (tails +30-40ms). looks like overlap decreased. excerpt:

```
NVTX Ranges:
step 102: matmul 12.3ms | allreduce start + 8.2ms | allreduce duration 18.7ms | kv-cache write 2.1ms
step 103: matmul 11.9ms | allreduce start + 5.0ms | allreduce duration 22.5ms | kv-cache write 1.9ms
step 104: matmul 14.1ms | allreduce start + 14.6ms | allreduce duration 25.3ms | kv-cache write 2.0ms
```

maya.g: PS — the runtime picked a different GEMM kernel for one of the layers (fp16 tiny tiling) after enabling checkpointing. suspecting different launch timing also affects all-reduce scheduling.

samir: interesting. hypothesis: activation checkpointing adds extra recompute kernels which shift the all-reduce windows, reducing compute/comm overlap. also if kernels are smaller/longer it can increase contention on the NIC due to fragmentation of collectives.

jordan: can we rule out KV cache interactions? checkpointing can change memory pressure and evictions. if KV cache writes are happening earlier/later maybe they block the host thread that launches collectives.

maya.g: good call. i captured host-thread trace too — saw occasional host-side stalls waiting on cuda events right before the all-reduce. snippet from host trace:

```
[host] sync_event wait (stream 2)  -> 3.7ms
[host] launch allreduce (step 104) at t+14.6ms
[host] kv cache flush sync: 1.9ms (stream 3)
```

alex.k: ok. experiments we can run: (1) force the old GEMM kernel to verify kernel selection effect (2) disable kv-cache writes for a few steps (3) disable activation checkpointing only across pipeline-stage boundaries to see if boundary recompute is the main culprit.

samir: i can run (1) and (3) on a small cluster. also add measurement of per-step allreduce duration and the time between collectives (to see overlap slack).

maya.g: added an instrumentation patch to the runtime — it emits per-collective NVTX + simple CSV metrics. dropping it to nightly now.

infra-bot: deploy-job: test/pp-tp-checkpointing-comm-analysis started (job id: 87932).

jordan: one more thought: our batching heuristic sometimes increases batch size when compute increases because it assumes better throughput. checkpointing inflates compute but may reduce overlap, so heuristics should consider collectives/tail latency, not only raw FLOPS. we should add a check to simulate collectives when estimating batch throughput.

alex.k: agreed. long term we need the optimizer to prefer kernels that improve overlap even if single-kernel latency is slightly higher. short term: samir — can you run the forced-kernel + disable-kv-cache experiment and paste the CSV output here?

samir: will run now, should have 10 steps of CSV in ~30m. planning to compare columns: step, matmul_ms, recompute_ms, allreduce_ms, kv_write_ms, host_stall_ms, chosen_kernel_tag.

maya.g: thanks — if we confirm it's overlap/regrouping, we should add a guard in the checkpointing path: avoid checkpoint across pipeline boundaries or adjust kernel selection for boundary layers.

alex.k: also file a perf run ticket for the Optimize team to add a metric for collectives overlap in the console. makes debug easier for customers.

jordan: noted — ticket created INF-4821 with the summary + links to traces.

samir: uploaded preliminary CSV: 
```
step,matmul_ms,recompute_ms,allreduce_ms,kv_write_ms,host_stall_ms,chosen_kernel_tag
1,11.8,4.2,18.9,2.0,0.5,gemm_fp16_tiling_A
2,12.1,4.1,19.5,1.9,0.6,gemm_fp16_tiling_A
3,14.0,6.0,25.6,2.1,3.8,gemm_fp16_small_tile_B
4,13.5,5.5,24.8,2.0,2.6,gemm_fp16_small_tile_B
```

samir: pattern looks consistent: steps using small_tile_B have longer allreduce and host_stall spikes.

maya.g: thanks — that's convincing. next steps: (a) force large-tile kernel for boundary layers (b) tweak batching heuristic to penalize observed host_stall_ms in simulation (c) add a short-term runtime fallback: if allreduce tails exceed threshold, fall back to non-checkpointed or adjusted kernel set for next few steps.

alex.k: sounds good. assign owners: samir -> (a) kernel forcing test + perf patch, jordan -> (b) batching heuristic change draft, maya.g -> (c) runtime fallback prototype. please update INF-4821 with progress.

jordan: adding draft PR for batching sim later today.

maya.g: will monitor nightly with instrumentation and report back in the morning. thx all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: job 87932 finished: SUCCESS (artifacts: nvtx-trace.zip, csv/pp-ckpt-87932.csv)

alex.k: great, wrap up and sync on Monday's runtime sync for rollout decision.
